sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Novus is a real loyalty-platform and rewards operator, but it is not economically equivalent to a pure SaaS company. Most reported sales are voucher and redemption flows. Bank integrations, low receivables and FY26 operating profit growth are positives; unresolved related-party reporting, the quality of cash conversion and the funding of a much larger proposed AutoPe purchase are decisive limitations.

Classification: **Hold — unresolved**. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are all NS, not zero or average scores. This is a speculative platform/inorganic-growth research situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. The dated secondary ₹192 quote supports arithmetic, not an investment recommendation. A funded standalone-only scenario can look attractive, but it excludes the very acquisition that could change cash, ownership and risk. Ordinary expected returns and entry prices remain unscored. Resolve the auditor/related-party and transaction-funding questions before price becomes the deciding variable. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company sells and operates loyalty technology, managed redemption, merchant promotions and digital vouchers. Technology includes implementation/customization and recurring support or hosted usage. Redemption combines a reward catalogue, sourcing margin and convenience fees. Merchant services link offers to enterprise users. Digital vouchers are procured through processor/brand APIs and sold in bulk, generally after receiving customer payment. Bank on-premises implementations coexist with hosted SaaS; software capability is not the same as software revenue. [S01](https://www.novus-loyalty.com/pdf/prospectus_novus.pdf) [S12](https://www.novus-loyalty.com/pdf/disclosure_regulation/Novus_Transcript_H2FY26.pdf)

| Period | Technology ₹cr | Redemption ₹cr | Merchant ₹cr | Voucher ₹cr | Exports ₹cr |

| FY23 | 6.7430 | 28.3605 | 3.3966 | 21.0940 | 10.9062 |
| FY24 | 7.0072 | 31.8599 | 3.5034 | 30.9213 | 6.4825 |
| FY25 | 7.2384 | 46.1465 | 6.4836 | 44.7563 | 2.2859 |

October management materials put FY26 gross sales mix at 7%,39%,6%,48% respectively. These rounded percentages are not multiplied into invented audited segment revenues. Voucher gross margin is described as 5–7%, and redemption margins vary by category. Neither is a company-wide net take rate: payroll, cloud, software development, marketing and other operating costs must still be paid. Management’s “70% product” capability language is not a 70% software revenue claim. The exact October revised copy has a dating limitation, so these claims are not used to score growth. sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest moat mechanism is integration friction: bank IT, security reviews, loyalty rules and embedded customer journeys are costly to change. Cross-selling a redemption catalogue through an existing installation may have a low marginal selling cost. Novus owns its product IP; the Parahit collaboration does not transfer ownership to the development vendor. That is a useful asset, not proof of monopoly economics. [S01](https://www.novus-loyalty.com/pdf/prospectus_novus.pdf) [S12](https://www.novus-loyalty.com/pdf/disclosure_regulation/Novus_Transcript_H2FY26.pdf)

Against this, customer concentration is high, vouchers are sourced from a small supplier set and the enterprise customer can tender or renegotiate. There is no verified net revenue retention, gross retention, renewal pricing or multi-cohort contribution history. User counts, processed transactions, AI branding and awards are not equivalent to proprietary network effects. The loss of a bank may remove both software and attached transaction economics.

| Peer | Why relevant | Why not a direct multiple twin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services | Rewards, gift-card procurement and program fees; FY26 standalone gross margin 45.4%, reported EBITDA margin 9.7%. | Much larger spend-management/card ecosystem with program-fee, incentive and ESOP accounting; not a pure software-sales multiple comparator. Use gross profit and cash earnings after incentives; do not equate gross Propel sales with recurring SaaS fees. |
| Capillary Technologies India | Enterprise loyalty and customer-engagement platform with recurring-revenue and retention disclosure. | Global acquisition-led cloud-software exposure, integration and stock compensation differ from Novus gross redemption flows. Ask Novus for equivalent ARR/retention definitions rather than importing a Capillary revenue multiple. |
| Easyrewardz | Private cloud CRM/loyalty competitor serving retail and BFSI customers. | No verified public-market valuation or comparable audited financial series used. Demonstrates credible functional competition; product breadth alone is not a moat. |

The comparison establishes competition and disclosure benchmarks. No current peer trading multiple is invented. Zaggle’s redemption/program-fee mix illustrates why gross-sales comparisons mislead; Capillary’s recurring metrics are a more demanding software benchmark; Easyrewardz is a functional competitor without a verified public valuation used here. MOAT5 reflects integration strengths alongside limited pricing-power evidence. Revenue additions are embedded for each annual row; FY26 growth over FY25 is 21.8%. Technology revenue increased only from ₹6.7430 crore to ₹7.2384 crore during FY23–25, about 3.6% annual growth. Exports fell sharply as legacy overseas/custom work wound down, while domestic reward/redemption activity expanded. That change is economically different from uniformly recurring software expansion. H1FY26 revenue ₹71.4087 crore is not annualized; the first half already represents roughly 56% of FY26 sales.

A reproducible value-added proxy subtracts direct costs and inventory movement from revenue. It is not audited net revenue or a segment gross-profit measure. FY25 direct costs contain about ₹4.31 crore software development, while that direct line is absent in FY26. Moving development between direct and other costs changes the proxy without changing true economics. Without comparable annual net-fee/contribution allocation, REV remains NS rather than applying the headline growth schedule to pass-through volume. sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth must come from more billable enterprise programs, deeper redemption usage, higher retained fees or a successful adjacent product, not simply larger voucher denominations. The existing enterprise footprint is a route to market. Central Bank’s announced ₹88 crore three-year engagement is usage-dependent and includes service/redemption economics; it is neither guaranteed annual recurring software revenue nor ₹88 crore incremental revenue in a single year. The standalone base scenario grows gross sales 18% annually, holds contribution margin near FY26 and grows existing operating costs 8%. It additionally expenses product spending ₹6.5 crore in each of FY27/FY28 and new marketing ₹4.8124 crore annually, rather than treating IPO spending as free. Thereafter product maintenance continues at ₹3 crore with 8% escalation and marketing continues with 8% escalation. Capex remains 0.5% of revenue and operating working capital 20 days. This is an explicit scenario, not a claim that customer counts, average fees or conversion rates have been verified.

The base therefore requires retained contribution, not merely gross sales, to scale enough to cover recurring investment. The bull case requires 25% growth and 31% contribution margin; the bear case 8% and 25%. No authoritative customer/fee cohort bridge or accessible market share has been disclosed to certify these outcomes. A global TAM would not repair that missing evidence.

GQS is NS with 45% evidence coverage. The cash-quality and capital-return constraints are not offset by a large order headline. The persistent weak-cash ceiling is evaluated explicitly, not ignored because the composite is missing. AutoPe’s target economics and ownership are a separate branch: acquisition spend cannot be justified using standalone ROCE while leaving acquired capital out of the denominator.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
1. **Retained economics disappoint.** Gross vouchers grow while software fees or retained margins stagnate. Product and marketing expenses then consume cash despite rising reported sales. The standalone bear case remains funded under its assumptions but destroys much of equity value through low earning power and a 10x exit, not merely a temporary quoted drawdown.
2. **Acquisition financing changes the claim.** A large cash deal can consume IPO reserves and require new equity/debt. Rescue financing can make the company survive while materially diluting existing shareholders. Target PAT cannot be fully attributed to Novus at 54.873% or 80.87%, and target cash is not freely transferable. Without target accounts, minority claims and financing terms, a combined fair value is NS.
3. **Stewardship/reliability fails to improve.** Unreconciled related advances and audit clauses can become a permanent recovery/minority-rights problem. Documented non-compliance is already adverse evidence, but a future loss is not asserted as certain.
4. **Concentration and supply dependence interact.** Loss of one anchor bank reduces both platform fees and attached transactions; supplier repricing can compress thin resale economics. Low receivable days do not eliminate franchise risk.
5. **Cash looks stronger than recurring earnings.** Related-claim collections, old payables and IPO funding can disguise weak future free cash. Statutory liabilities, tax payments and product costs must be paid even if growth slows.
6. **Exit liquidity fails.** A1,000-share lot, narrow book and circuit restrictions can prevent selling when fundamental risk appears. A falling quote does not guarantee a buyer or eventual recovery.

The main permanent-loss pathway is a jointly adverse margin/customer shock and expensive, diluted acquisition funded before benefits arrive. Recovery depends on actual recurring customer contribution, recoverable related claims, disciplined capital allocation and a financeable balance sheet, not a peer SaaS multiple. No precise probability is assigned to such correlated outcomes. sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger target is not central to this unresolved research thesis. Over the exact five-year horizon,5× requires approximately 37.9% annual shareholder return and 10× requires 58.4%. At an unchanged share count, those outcomes mean ₹960/₹1,920 per share and roughly ₹1492.82/₹2985.64 crore equity value.

The conditional standalone base produces about 2.71× terminal wealth and the deliberately optimistic bull about 7.07×. The bull assumes 25% gross revenue growth,31% contribution margin and 22× terminal EBIT, with all modeled product/marketing and capital needs paid. It is a possible scenario, not evidence that 5× is likely;10× is not reached in these cases.

A durable 5×/10× case would require comparable net-fee growth, sustainable retained margins and incremental returns, and verified acquisition financing without per-share dilution erasing value. Unknown ESOPs or rescue shares increase the total equity value required for the same per-share outcome. Do not conflate target enterprise value, partially owned target profit or the company’s gross transaction growth with shareholder wealth. Ordinary multibagger feasibility remainsNS while the gates are unresolved.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
**Hold — unresolved.** Descriptive research supports a functioning business with bank integration advantages and improved FY26 operating earnings. It does not yet support the same economics as a recurring-software compounder, a dependable current funding bridge or a ranking-quality investment return.

Business Quality: NS. Growth Quality: NS. Investment Attractiveness: NS. Numerical quality, growth and investment rankings are all ineligible. This is not an “Avoid — governance” verdict because the evidence supports GOV4/Hold rather than proven severe abuse or GOV≤3; it is also not a Buy justified by subtracting all IPO cash from market capitalization. Ordinary return and entry price remain null.

What could change the stance: consistent auditor/RPT reconciliation; final related-advance remediation; comparable retained/net-fee growth and cash conversion; executed AutoPe price, ownership and committed financing; exact option dilution; and verified BSE tradability. The conditional standalone valuation is useful for disciplined discussion once those facts are available, not a substitute for them.

methodology: Dates are half-open intervals from1Apr2026 to20Oct2031; entry20Oct2026 and terminal20Oct2031. Fiscal denominators365/366 and equity horizon1826/365; no post-terminal funding.

Old taxes, statutory obligations, expense payables and employee provisions settled once on30Apr2026; income-tax assets and director claims assigned no recovery. GST adverse settlement net of predeposit included once. Remaining IPO budget minus incurred cost charged once; no second deduction of incurred IPO fees already within cash/equity/old payables.

All incremental product expenditure expensed. Recurring marketing continues after IPO budget expiry and product maintenance continues at3cr plus8% annual escalation. Base opex also grows; revenue does not stand in for cash earnings.
Seller acquisition payments are cash leaving the group; target bank balances cannot fund parent absent a legal distribution. Acquisition values are not asserted from uncertain target accounts.

summary:
Novus is a real loyalty-platform and rewards operator, but it is not economically equivalent to a pure SaaS company. Most reported sales are voucher and redemption flows. Bank integrations, low receivables and FY26 operating profit growth are positives; unresolved related-party reporting, the quality of cash conversion and the funding of a much larger proposed AutoPe purchase are decisive limitations.

Classification: **Hold — unresolved**. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are all NS, not zero or average scores. This is a speculative platform/inorganic-growth research situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. The dated secondary ₹192 quote supports arithmetic, not an investment recommendation. A funded standalone-only scenario can look attractive, but it excludes the very acquisition that could change cash, ownership and risk. Ordinary expected returns and entry prices remain unscored. Resolve the auditor/related-party and transaction-funding questions before price becomes the deciding variable.
